title: Grade 4 HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — Termly Exam #15 (Term 3)

pages.quiz:
HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — TERMLY EXAM #15 (TERM 3)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What does Artha mean? (1 mark)
   A. Honest wealth and the things we need
   B. War
   C. A river
   D. Prayer

2. What does Kama mean? (1 mark)
   A. A festival
   B. Good and healthy wishes such as joy and friendship
   C. War
   D. Cruelty

3. Which tradition teaches the five principles in this lesson? (1 mark)
   A. Only the Buddhist tradition
   B. A trade union
   C. Sanatan or Vedic
   D. A market

4. According to Hindu belief, what does the soul do after death? (1 mark)
   A. Turns into a tree only
   B. Turns to stone
   C. Ends forever
   D. Takes a new body

5. Which of the five principles is about goals? (1 mark)
   A. Paramatma
   B. Punarjanam
   C. Prarthana
   D. Purushartha

6. How does Namaste show the idea of Paramatma? (1 mark)
   A. It means goodbye only
   B. It is a race
   C. It is a food
   D. It shows respect for the divine in everyone

7. Which festival comes last of the three studied? (1 mark)
   A. Madaraka Day
   B. Paryushan Parva
   C. Yoga Day
   D. Maha Shivratri

8. Which prayer is chanted on Maha Shivratri? (1 mark)
   A. Ee Mungu Nguvu Yetu
   B. Om Namah Shivaya
   C. Micchami Dukkadam
   D. Ik Onkar

9. On which date did Kenya become fully independent? (1 mark)
   A. 21 June 2015
   B. 12 December 1963
   C. 1 June 1963
   D. 1 January 1964

10. Which festival in the lesson is celebrated near the middle of the year on 1 June? (1 mark)
   A. Yoga Day
   B. Madaraka Day
   C. Paryushan
   D. Maha Shivratri

11. Which mistake is common about Maha Shivratri? (1 mark)
   A. Knowing it is for Shiva
   B. Thinking it is the same as Diwali
   C. Knowing it is in Phalguna
   D. Knowing about fasting

12. What does Utsav mean? (1 mark)
   A. Festival
   B. Yoga
   C. River
   D. Prayer

13. How should we behave when the National Anthem is sung? (1 mark)
   A. Play
   B. Talk
   C. Stand straight and be quiet
   D. Run about

14. Which is a good food safety rule? (1 mark)
   A. Share used cups
   B. Eat with dirty hands
   C. Leave food in the sun
   D. Wash hands before eating

15. What is Madaraka Day? (1 mark)
   A. A Hindu festival
   B. A Kenyan national holiday on 1 June
   C. A sports day
   D. A Jain festival

16. What is the Panchang? (1 mark)
   A. The Indian traditional calendar book
   B. A river
   C. A kind of tree
   D. A prayer

17. What is a calendar? (1 mark)
   A. A festival
   B. A prayer
   C. A way of counting days, weeks and months
   D. A kind of map

18. What does the Moon do in modern science? (1 mark)
   A. It is a planet
   B. It goes around Mars
   C. It is a star
   D. It goes around the Earth

19. Which day is linked with Mars? (1 mark)
   A. Thursday
   B. Saturday
   C. Friday
   D. Tuesday

20. Shani is the Indian name for which planet? (1 mark)
   A. Saturn
   B. Mars
   C. Jupiter
   D. Venus

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Explain how the story of Prahlad shows faith in Paramatma. (3 marks)

22. Write a short composition on a festival of your choice. (5 marks)

23. Describe how to pray well. (4 marks)

24. Describe what the Panchang is. (2 marks)

25. Write the Indian names for Sunday and Monday. (2 marks)

26. Name two grahas in the traditional calendar that are not planets in modern science. (2 marks)

27. Give three uses of the Indian traditional calendar. (3 marks)

28. Why do the festival dates in this calendar change from year to year on our usual calendar? (2 marks)

29. Explain the four Purusharthas with one example each for a child. (4 marks)

30. Write three ways in which a child can practise Prani Daya. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — TERMLY EXAM #15 (TERM 3) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — Honest wealth and the things we need
   Artha is earning in an honest way.

2. B — Good and healthy wishes such as joy and friendship
   Kama is good and healthy desire.

3. C — Sanatan or Vedic
   It is the ancient Hindu way.

4. D — Takes a new body
   This is rebirth.

5. D — Purushartha
   Goals of life.

6. D — It shows respect for the divine in everyone
   Namaste honours the divine in others.

7. B — Paryushan Parva
   It occurs in August or September.

8. B — Om Namah Shivaya
   It is a well-known prayer to Shiva.

9. B — 12 December 1963
   Jamhuri Day is 12 December.

10. B — Madaraka Day
   1 June is mid-year.

11. B — Thinking it is the same as Diwali
   They are different festivals.

12. A — Festival
   Utsav means festival.

13. C — Stand straight and be quiet
   We show respect.

14. D — Wash hands before eating
   Hygiene is important.

15. B — A Kenyan national holiday on 1 June
   It celebrates self-government.

16. A — The Indian traditional calendar book
   It lists days, months and festival dates.

17. C — A way of counting days, weeks and months
   Calendars organise time.

18. D — It goes around the Earth
   The Moon is Earth's natural satellite.

19. D — Tuesday
   Mangalvaar.

20. A — Saturn
   Shani is Saturn.

SECTION B
----
21. (3 marks)
   Answer: Prahlad believed God is everywhere, kept praying when his father was angry, and was protected.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

22. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any well-organised composition naming the festival, when it is held, what people do, what it teaches and how you feel.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for name, timing, activities, meaning, and feeling.

23. (4 marks)
   Answer: Sit quietly, fold hands, think of God with love, say thanks, ask for wisdom and kindness, and end with a promise to do good (any four).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

24. (2 marks)
   Answer: The Indian traditional calendar book that lists days, months and festival dates.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for two points.

25. (2 marks)
   Answer: Sunday: Ravivaar. Monday: Somvaar.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

26. (2 marks)
   Answer: The Sun and the Moon.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

27. (3 marks)
   Answer: Fixing festival dates, choosing days for prayers and family events, keeping tradition alive (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

28. (2 marks)
   Answer: The months follow the Moon, so the dates move.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

29. (4 marks)
   Answer: Dharma: doing homework and telling the truth. Artha: saving pocket money honestly. Kama: enjoying play and friendship. Moksha: praying and growing kind.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct pair.

30. (3 marks)
   Answer: Give water to thirsty animals, share food, help a hurt friend, do not harm insects, care for plants (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.
